message: Fabio Aru takes the Tour’s yellow jersey after Chris Froome falters in the Pyrenees.

description: Government’s stance of ‘keep calm and carry on’ raises questions in Brussels and among British businesses over its vision of future ties.
message: British government ministers are apparently keeping calm and carrying onin the face of the many challenges posed by Brexit negotiations, showing a lack of urgency that bewilders Brussels, Stephen Fidler writes.

description: Janet Yellen is an unlikely Goldilocks, but the Fed chairwoman has finally chased the three bears away from emerging markets. A jump in EM stocks and currencies after her slightly dovish comments Wednesday offers key lessons.
message: A jump in emerging market stocks and currencies after Yellen’s testimony offers three lessons, writes James Mackintosh.

description: U.S. President Donald Trump and his French counterpart, Emmanuel Macron, lavished praise on one another in a pointed effort to move past the deep divisions on display at last week’s Group of 20 summit.
message: Donald Trump and Emmanuel Macron use Paris meeting to signal comity in face of differences on trade and climate.

description: The state’s Attorney General’s Office has begun a criminal investigation into a prestigious boarding school that has been under scrutiny for allegations of past sexual abuse and conquest games on campus.
message: The New Hampshire Attorney General’s Office has begun a criminal investigation into St. Paul’s School, a prestigious New England boarding school that has been under scrutiny for allegations of past sexual abuse and conquest games on campus.

description: A recipe for renewed trade tensions: Donald Trump facing difficulties at home, China failing to rein in North Korea and a sharply rising trade deficit.
message: Question: When political leaders get into trouble at home, what is their favorite strategy for deflecting attention? Answer: Blame the foreigners.

description: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Liu Xiaobo, who embodied the hopes of the 1989 Tiananmen Square democracy movement, died on July 13 while serving an 11-year prison sentence for inciting subversion. Photo: AFP/Getty.
message: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Liu Xiaobo, who embodied the hopes of the 1989 Tiananmen Square democracy movement, died on July 13 while serving an 11-year prison sentence for inciting subversion.

description: The federal judge ruled President Donald Trump’s strict approach in implementing a temporary ban on U.S. entry for some travelers from six Muslim-majority countries contradicted a recent Supreme Court ruling.
message: The decision is a fresh legal blow for the president just two weeks after a Supreme Court ruling allowed the administration to implement its travel ban against refugees and foreign nationals from six countries who have no connection to the U.S.

description: A string of agricultural overhauls has set up China to import more grains and other commodities, with significant consequences for global markets. Farmers from Brazil to the U.S. and Thailand stand to benefit.
message: China needs more foreign grains and other commodities. Farmers in the U.S. should be pleased about this.

description: Peter W. Smith, a Republican political activist and financier from Chicago who mounted an effort to obtain former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton’s emails from Russian hackers, died on May 14 after asphyxiating himself in a hotel room in Rochester, Minn.
message: Peter W. Smith, a Republican political activist and financier from Chicago who mounted an effort to obtain former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton’s emails from Russian hackers, died on May 14 after asphyxiating himself in a hotel room.

description: Nobel Peace laureate Liu Xiaobo, who embodied the hopes of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Square democracy movement long after the protests were crushed, died while still under police guard after a battle with liver cancer at 61 years old.
message: A look back at the life of Liu Xiaobo in pictures.

description: Beijing said a 10.5% rise in its trade with Pyongyang in the first half of the year was part of a normal economic relationship with its neighbor.
message: China says it is abiding by U.N. sanctions on North Korea—but its trade with Pyongyang has risen.

description: One of China’s most prolific overseas acquirers, the airlines-to-hotels conglomerate HNA Group, is drastically slowing its deal making, suggesting a government crackdown on debt may be crimping its global ambitions.
message: HNA, one of China’s most prolific overseas acquirers, plans to slow its deal making.

description: Tributes to Chinese Nobel Peace laureate and democracy icon Liu Xiaobo poured out across the globe following his death, and calls that had focused on letting him seek treatment outside China shifted to his widow’s right to leave the country.
message: “With his passing, a monument of the Chinese people’s relentless struggle for freedom has been erected.”

description: The Congressional Budget Office estimates President Trump’s budget proposal would shrink deficits by nearly a third over the coming decade, but not nearly as much as the White House projects.
message: Under the Trump budget, the federal deficit would total $720 billion in fiscal 2027, the CBO says. That compares to a $16 billion surplus estimated by the White House.

description: They face re-election in states Trump won. Will they cozy up or join the ‘resistance’?
message: WSJ Opinion: Republicans must show voters that these Democrats say one thing during elections and something else in between them, writes Karl Rove.

description: Secretary of State Rex Tillerson called Thursday on Qatar and four other Arab nations to meet directly to end a feud between the crucial U.S. allies now in its second month.
message: Secretary of State Rex Tillerson urges Qatar and four other Arab nations to meet directly to end a feud between the crucial U.S. allies.

description: In their final days in Mosul, Islamic State militants dispatched dozens of suicide bombers—including women with babies in their arms—and searched homes for young boys they could force into battle, said Iraqi commanders who led the fight and residents who survived.
message: Toward the end of the Mosul battle, Islamic State deployed about 60 suicide bombers a day, one Iraqi commander said.

description: President Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the Federal Bureau of Investigation looks poised to draw significant Democratic support in the Senate, giving him a bipartisan show of confidence at a politically sensitive time for the nation’s top law enforcement agency.
message: Trump’s nominee to lead the FBI, Christopher Wray, looks poised to draw significant Democratic support in Senate.

description: The Trump agenda for achieving 3% economic growth.
message: WSJ Opinion: The focus of MAGAnomics is simple: Grow the economy and with it the wealth of, and opportunity for, all Americans, writes Director of the Office of Management and Budget Mick Mulvaney.

description: President Donald Trump is touting policies to boost U.S. energy production and exports as a bulwark against Russia, but experts say they would have limited impact on Russia as a major energy provider.
message: Trump is touting his policies to boost energy production and exports as a bulwark against Russia, but experts say the U.S. shale boom has only limited impact on Russia’s standing as a major energy provider to Europe and Asia.

description: President Donald Trump, who is struggling to win congressional approval for his promised border wall with Mexico, now says that the project doesn’t have to stretch along the entire southern border.
message: Struggling to win approval for his border wall, the president says the project doesn’t have to stretch along the entire southern border.

description: Investors are diving into overseas stock funds while ditching expectations for a rebound in the dollar, the latest market ripple of the greenback’s surprise 2017 slide.
message: Investors are diving into overseas stock funds while giving up on a dollar rebound.

description: Some federal hospital funding likely to be slashed in a health-care overhaul could be restored under the revised GOP health bill—but to qualify, hospitals in states that expanded Medicaid must first roll the expansion back.
message: More hospitals could get some federal payments back under the new GOP bill—but there’s a catch.

description: Princeton scientists coated a piece of glass with a laminate that will turn the panel dark blue on command.
message: The scientists say such windows could cut our energy bills. They could also improve privacy with a version that would get so dark that people couldn’t see in or out.
Too tired to bother cooking after work tonight? This "smart" oven can make you a proper dinner—on its own.

description: Top a summer fruit pie with a simple lattice of just a few pastry strips or opt for a more intricate weave. Follow these simple illustrated steps to get started. Plus, a recipe for peach pie.
message: Impressive as it looks, a lattice-top pie doesn't have to be hard to pull off.

description: It was a speech about values and traditions that neither Hillary Clinton nor any Democrat would give anymore.
message: WSJ Opinion: The Trump “base” knew the 2016 presidential election was a crucial event, deciding whether America would go on in the Western tradition as it was developed in the U.S. or continue its steady drift away from those ideas, writes Daniel Henninger.

description: While the nation’s capitol withers and sweats under a July heat-wave, House Speaker Paul Ryan hinted he would soon help reporters and congressional staff stay cool.
message: The rules aren’t often enforced for lawmakers, but the dress code is enforced by security guards who turn away ladies in sleeveless dresses or tops and gentlemen not wearing a jacket and tie.

description: Dan Neil puts the McLaren 720S to the test on the perilously windy roads of Wales.
message: The 720S defies you to understand how it cools, breathes or stays on the ground. It seems built to fly in a different wind.

description: F. William McNabb III plans to step down as chief executive of Vanguard Group after leading the indexing pioneer through a decade when it emerged as the world’s second-largest money manager.
message: Under departing CEO McNabb, Vanguard transformed from a low-cost manager of $1.25 trillion in assets to one with $4.4 trillion in assets under management, trailing only BlackRock.

description: A look at some tricky anomalies; why most of us can see prices rise even as the average falls.
message: Consider a hotel with 100 reasonably priced rooms and one exorbitant suite going for $50,000 a night. If the price of the standard rooms all go up by $10 but the penthouse rate falls by more than $1,000, the mean will go down, although we ordinary folk won’t feel it.

description: The president’s moves are neither capricious nor naive, though they lack a certain diplomatic finesse.
message: WSJ Opinion: Chinese leaders have long been accustomed to strong words and no action from Washington; now they will have to consider how far the Trump administration may go.

description: Roku Inc., which makes streaming media devices and software, is preparing an initial public offering it expects to launch before year-end, according to people familiar with the company’s plans.
message: Roku is prepping an IPO, and the maker of streaming devices is seeking a valuation around $1 billion.

description: The conclusion of a trilogy in the simian-human series crosses extravagant action with complex themes.
message: The apes are the good guys here, but the humans who made the movie do our species proud, writes Joe Morgenstern.

description: Do you reflexively dismiss Riesling as a sweet wine? Don’t: Dry, crisp Rieslings abound, in winemaking regions around the world. Here, a few superb choices.
message: The many types and styles of Riesling range from extremely dry to extremely sweet; there’s sparkling Riesling too.

description: In our search for the ultimate luxury pool float, we left no cushion unturned. Rigorous reviews of the Pigro Felice Modul’Air, Oasis Pool Lounger, Kai Float and Aqua Lounger.
message: In our search for the ultimate luxury pool float, we left no cushion unturned. A rigorous review of four high-end floating loungers:

description: In Thursday’s Emmy nominations, ‘The Crown,’ ‘The Handmaid’s Tale,’ ‘Stranger Things,’ ‘This Is Us’ and ‘Westworld’ were first-time nominees for Outstanding Drama Series.
message: “The Crown” ( Netflix ), “The Handmaid’s Tale” (Hulu), “Stranger Things” (Netflix), “This Is Us” (NBC) and “Westworld” (HBO) were first-time nominees for Outstanding Drama Series.

description: Global investors seem nearly as skeptical as Trump partisans.
message: WSJ Opinion: The world’s investors still like U.S. equities, despite constant media reports that U.S. constitutional governance is hanging in the balance.

description: President Donald Trump backed his eldest son’s decision last June to accept a meeting to discuss what was described as a Russian government offer of allegedly damaging information about Democrat Hillary Clinton.
message: President Trump defended Donald Jr. during a speech in France, saying, "Most people would’ve taken that meeting."

description: Smartphone out of memory...again? Three free and paid ways to easily copy your photos and videos to the cloud.
message: Free up memory on your phone with these photo backup plans.

description: The Federal Communications Commission opened a new inquiry into ways to curb unwanted robocalls Thursday, with the aim of deterring use of fake phone numbers--a tactic known as spoofing that has been a major factor in the current epidemic.
message: Cracking down on robocalls and spoofing remains tricky, because phone companies generally are obligated to complete calls.

description: The U.K. government published its first draft legislation on Brexit since a June election cost Prime Minister Theresa May her parliamentary majority, marking the first step in what looks set to be a bitterly fought domestic battle
message: The proposals in the draft legislation would end the supremacy of EU law in British courts after Brexit—a key goal of leaving—and allow Parliament to keep, alter or ditch the 19,000 EU laws currently enforceable in the U.K.

description: The Congressional Budget Office estimates President Donald Trump’s budget proposal would shrink deficits by nearly a third over the coming decade, but not nearly as much as the White House projects.
message: Under the Trump budget, the federal deficit would total $720 billion by 2027, compared with a $16 billion surplus estimated by the White House, the CBO said in an analysis of the president’s budget.

description: Research shows that Facebook social networks can play a role in—and possibly enhance—intimacy and grieving after the loss of a close friend.
message: Online social networks may provide us with means to lessen loneliness far more varied than those of a few decades ago.

description: Senate GOP leaders released revised legislation that would topple parts of the Affordable Care Act, impose steep cuts on Medicaid and allow insurers to sell cheaper plans that don’t meet the current law’s regulations.
message: Letting insurers offer basic, cheap health plans would lead healthy people to buy them rather than the more comprehensive and expensive plans.

description: Shares in the U.K. drug giant fell sharply after a news outlet reported he was moving to lead Teva Pharmaceuticals, an Israeli generics drugmaker that has been looking for a new chief for months.
message: Is AstraZeneca's CEO staying or going?

description: Canadian insurer Manulife Financial is exploring a possible initial public offering or spinoff of its John Hancock Financial Services unit.
message: Manulife has been under pressure from some of its shareholders to sell John Hancock after years of disappointing returns from the U.S. unit, according to two people familiar with the company.

description: CBS News and BBC News have entered into a partnership to share video, articles and other newsgathering resources to enhance their reporting capabilities around the world.
message: The new deal ends longstanding relationships that CBS had with Sky PLC’s Sky News and that ABC News had with the BBC.

description: After launching in 2011, ride-hailing app Yandex.Taxi all but ended the traditional Russian practice of flagging down any car driver wanting to earn a few extra rubles. Now, it has seen off another competitor: Uber Technologies Inc.
message: The arrival of Uber in Moscow in 2014 sparked a price war with a local ride-hailing app. Now they have joined forces.

description: Bastide, owned by Fekkai and his wife Shirin von Wulffen, opens its first flagship boutique in Aix-en-Provence.
message: The beauty of Bastide.

description: Greek carrier DryShips sold vast sums of discounted shares to an offshore firm and propped up prices with “reverse splits,” sending investors on a wild ride that, for many, ended with steep losses.
message: The Greek carrier DryShips sold vast sums of discounted shares to an offshore firm and propped up prices with ‘reverse splits,’ sending investors on a wild ride that, for many, ended in ruin.

description: The most popular photos on three major home and design websites show what consumers love in home design.
message: WSJ's Mansion section asked the editors of three home-centric websites—Houzz, BHG.com and HGTV.com—to identify their most popular images from the first half of 2017. These are the photos with the most online clicks, likes and saves.

description: South Carolina’s Daufuskie Island offers golf, nature and history without the crowds of nearby Hilton Head and Savannah. But developers have struggled to attract luxury homeowners to this sleepy enclave.
message: Daufuskie—an idyllic island that’s looking for luxury home-buyers.

description: U.S. prosecutors have charged more than 400 people with taking part in alleged health care fraud and opioid scams that totaled $1.3 billion in false billing.
message: Alleged opioid-prescription scams and other tactics amounted to $1.3 billion in false billings, U.S. says

description: South Korea says it is ready to discuss changes to its free-trade deal with the U.S. but won’t rush into renegotiations, after the Trump administration signaled it wants to modify the agreement.
message: Despite the Trump administration’s signals, Seoul indicates it won’t hurry into any renegotiation of the countries' free-trade agreement.

description: App settings that accelerate voices to 5x or more allow impatient listeners to finish hourlong episodes in minutes. ‘A presumably insane person.’
message: You've heard of speed-reading. This is about speed listening.

description: Stripping out irritating ad formats and limiting the number of ads forced on visitors can actually increase ad revenue, some publishers say.
message: Can fewer ads be good for business? Some web publishers say "less is more."

description: Target said rising store traffic helped turn comparable-store sales growth positive for the first time in a year, giving the retailer an early win in its bid to improve stores and lure shoppers.
message: Target gives a rosier outlook, helped by rising store traffic.

description: Brazil’s left-wing parties rallied around former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva after the metalworker turned working class hero was sentenced to almost a decade in prison for corruption, throwing plans for a grand political comeback into disarray.
message: The day after Brazil's former president was convicted, the country's left-wing parties are rallying around him.

There's a complex backstory to the $3 billion Apple-Beats deal. But Jimmy Iovine says his partnership with Dr Dre is "magic," and gives us a behind-the-scenes look at the making of "The Defiant Ones" on HBO.

description: Nobel Peace laureate Liu Xiaobo, who embodied the hopes of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Square democracy movement long after the protests were crushed, died while still under police guard after a battle with liver cancer at 61 years old.
message: Nobel laureate Liu Xiaobo, a Chinese pro-democracy organizer at Tiananmen and beyond, has died at 61.

description: New research suggests that since 2000, men who would otherwise be working are instead being drawn into immersive virtual worlds. The paper is being viewed cautiously at the Fed as part of the explanation for why male labor-force participation has been so weak.
message: America’s young men are increasingly giving up on work in order to slay virtual aliens and fight videogame wars.

description: A personal, guided tour to the best scoops and stories every day in The Wall Street Journal, from Editor in Chief Gerard Baker.
message:
Today's top stories: Gerard Baker on Trump's Russia defense, China's booming housing market and more. 
Sign up here for the daily newsletter: http://on.wsj.com/2uipfEo

description: Venezuela’s opposition plans to hold a vote Sunday in the hope of rejecting President Nicolás Maduro’s plan to dissolve the national legislature and possibly rewrite the constitution, giving him what critics say would be near-dictatorial powers.
message: Many Venezuelans say President Maduro's latest strategy would give him near-dictatorial powers.

description: The Kalashnikov rifle, or AK-47, is one of the most abundant firearms ever made. But the company behind the iconic weapon is fighting its own battles. WSJ's Niki Blasina reports. Photo: Niki Blasina/The Wall Street Journal
message: The company behind the AK-47 is fighting its own battles.

description: Shoppers’ retreat from department stores and mall chains is prompting stock traders to stalk the retail sector with a fervor unseen in years.
message: Hard times for traditional retailers is making for fertile ground for investors who buy unloved stocks.

description: It’s been more than five months since President Donald Trump declared that he was putting Iran “on notice.” For the Iranian regime, that is turning out to be a rather comfortable place, as a series of international events have combined to bolster Tehran’s influence, at least for now.
message: President Donald Trump put Iran "on notice" months ago, yet events since then have boosted Tehran's influence.

description: How can China expect to be a world power like the U.S. if it won't curb North Korea's nuclear enthusiasm?
message: China faces a moment of truth in its own backyard. So far, its approach on North Korea lines up poorly with its ambition to assume greater global leadership.

description: Russian arms manufacturer Kalashnikov Concern once had America in its sights, but sanctions imposed by the U.S. ended those plans. After a quick pivot, sales are booming as the company looks to Asia and Africa for new business.
message: How a Soviet-era rifle maker transformed itself into a global arms seller.

description: Uber Technologies is combining its Russian operations with Yandex.Taxi, a rare retreat that shows the beleaguered San Francisco company’s willingness to withdraw from costly battles abroad.
message: Uber is beating a rare retreat in Russia, showing the beleaguered company’s willingness to withdraw from costly battles abroad.

description: As auto makers such as GM and tech companies like Google and Apple rush to develop self-driving cars or their software, the world’s largest vehicle market—China—is creating roadblocks by limiting who can map its highways.
message: Why global car and tech firms worry they can’t compete in China with self-driving cars.

description: With the U.S. retail industry in a state of flux, American retailers and e-commerce companies should take a look at China, where companies have been weaving together the online and offline worlds.
message: "I came to the convenience store for convenience, not human interaction"—24-year-old Carson Zhang, a customer at a cashierless convenience store.

description: The government adopted new legislation that will make it easier for it to veto takeovers of strategically important companies, a move that effectively—though not nominally—targets China’s attempt to acquire key technology.
message: Germany is putting up barriers to protect its technology from Chinese suitors.

description: A 20% rise in the shares of HSBC this year and a 50% jump in Tencent have helped push the benchmark Hang Seng Index to its highest level in two years.
message: What's brought on Hong Kong's stock-market surge?

description: Indonesian President Joko Widodo has signed a decree giving his government the power to disband radical organizations, following months of sectarian tensions in the predominantly Muslim nation.
message: The growing influence of hard-line Islamist groups recently has undermined Indonesia’s reputation for practicing a moderate, tolerant form of the faith.

description: Theater postpones production based on life of Rudolf Nureyev amid questions about state censorship and homophobia.
message:
It was supposed to be the hottest ticket of Moscow’s theater season: A ballet based on the life of legendary dancer Rudolf Nureyev.

Instead, critics say it has become a casualty of Russia’s culture wars.

description: Analysis: In the age of Netflix movies, HBO TV shows and Marvel big-screen series, the 120-year-old definition of a feature film is defunct
message: R.I.P. movies?

description: The drug, called ACZ885, is already sold under the brand name Ilaris for certain rare inflammatory disorders affecting a very small number of people.
message: Novartis recently discovered that a drug it sells for a group of very rare diseases could be used to treat a much more common ailment. There is just one problem: its $16,000-per-dose price tag.

description: The U.S. leader is to be Bastille Day guest of honor at the invitation of French President Emmanuel Macron.
message: President Donald Trump is set to arrive in Paris Thursday morning for a whirlwind visit amid a political storm at home.

description: McConnell appears to have made little progress in bridging the deep divides imperiling his party’s seven-year quest to topple the Affordable Care Act.
message:
U.S. Senate Majority Leader McConnell faced intensifying pressure from President Trump, conservative lawmakers and outside groups to push through a health-care overhaul next week. 

Republicans plan to unveil Thursday the text of the latest version of their bill.

description: Iran’s ambitious agenda for its oil-and-gas industry is running up against the caution of big energy companies.
message: Iranian officials set out ambitious energy plans this year, but they are running into a problem: A Western oil industry still smarting from low oil prices is moving cautiously.

description: Asian tech giants, startups and auto makers, including Baidu, nuTonomy and Nissan, are aggressively pursuing driverless-vehicle technology. Photo: Getty Images
message: Asian tech giants, startups and auto makers, including Baidu, nuTonomy and Nissan, are aggressively pursuing driverless-vehicle technology.

description: For Martín Berasategui, the Basque chef who bagged his eighth Michelin star last year—the most of any chef in Spain—a recent revelation came in the form of a mud-caked beet.
message: Martín Berasategui has more Michelin stars than any other chef in Spain. But it’s at home, cooking for family, where he finds his center. Here, his tips on cookware, ingredients and how to make guests feel welcome.

description: The Cold War test of nerves is back. Risky close encounters between Russian and NATO forces have increased dramatically in the Baltic region over the past three years. WSJ's Tanya Rivero explains what's at stake.  Photo: U.S. Air Force/Associated Press
message: The Cold War test of nerves is back. Risky close encounters between Russian and NATO forces have increased dramatically in the Baltic region over the past three years. WSJ's Tanya Rivero explains what's at stake.

description: New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio declared war on rats, unveiling a $32 million initiative to sharply reduce the population of rodents that roam the city.
message: At $7,000 each, city officials said so-called smart trash cans are expensive but worth the investment.

description: Arson and looting in the guise of protest made Newark and Detroit what they are today.
message: WSJ Opinion: Arson and looting in the guise of protest made Newark and Detroit what they are today, writes Jason Riley.

description: Authorities in China released 10 employees of Australian casino company Crown Resorts after they were convicted of gambling offenses last month, in a closely watched case for the global casino industry.
message: Jason O’Connor, who led Crown’s international VIP program, remains in custody.

description: Does Scott Garrett want to lead the Ex-Im Bank or kill it?
message: WSJ Opinion: A quick look at Scott Garrett’s record as a congressman before he lost re-election last year shows his contempt for the Export-Important Bank, which he now seeks to lead, writes Jay Timmons.

description: Scientists reported Wednesday that an iceberg nearly the size of the state of Delaware broke off the Antarctic peninsula, changing the continent’s landscape in one of the largest such “calving” events in recent history.
message: Collapse of an entire ice shelf generally can be more problematic for sea levels because the shelves help prevent ice from the continent’s interior creeping toward the edge and into the sea.

description: President Donald Trump sought to refute allegations that the Russian government tried to help his presidential campaign and damage that of Hillary Clinton, arguing that his policies run counter to Kremlin’s interests.
message: In his comments to the Christian Broadcasting Network, President Trump suggested that his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, would have preferred that Hillary Clinton, the Democratic nominee, win the 2016 election. Mr. Trump alleged her stances on military and energy policy would have been more helpful to Moscow.

description: ISIS emerged in the vacuum the U.S. created by withdrawing in 2011. Don’t repeat that mistake.
message: WSJ Opinion: ISIS emerged in the vacuum the U.S. created by withdrawing in 2011. Don’t repeat that mistake.

description: In the surest signal yet that the Canadian economy has turned a corner after the oil-price shock, the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by a quarter percentage point, to 0.75%, its first increase in seven years.
message: Canada's improving economy has soaked up unused labor and production capacity at a “significant” pace, the bank said, and a string of improving indicators measuring employment, exports and business-investment intentions suggest the time has come for a rate rise.

description: A congressional battle over President Donald Trump’s nominations for a range of influential positions is escalating and becoming more acrimonious, creating additional uncertainty over when some notable government vacancies might be filled.
message: More than 30 nominees are sitting on the sidelines while they await a final Senate confirmation vote. Those include several picks for the Justice and Treasury departments, as well as new commissioners for a federal energy regulator that has been unable to conduct official business because of its vacancies.

description: The iPhone maker will begin storing all cloud data for its customers in China with a government-owned company—a move that means relinquishing some control over its data.
message: Under the new arrangement, all of the iCloud data for its customers in China will be stored in the country. Currently, Apple pulls some iCloud data for Chinese users from servers in the U.S.

description: Surprise, he didn’t run his campaign any smarter than his government.
message: WSJ Opinion: Donald Trump is not Nixon, and Watergate, in its antecedents, was more like the polar opposite of what is now befalling the Trump administration.

description: Royal Bank of Scotland agreed to pay $5.5 billion to a U.S. agency to settle a probe into its sale of toxic mortgage-backed securities in the runup to the financial crisis.
message: In settling, RBS becomes the 17th bank to strike a deal with the Federal Housing Finance Agency over the sale of subprime mortgages to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. The settlement came in higher than investors expected, tempering the idea that U.S. agencies would soften their approach to foreign banks under the Trump administration.

description: After having turned itself from a former Soviet republic into Europe’s undisputed digital leader in just 25 years, Estonia wants to use its EU presidency to export its e-citizen revolution to the rest of Europe, Simon Nixon writes.
message: Under Estonia's e-citizenship program, the government provides every citizen with a secure digital identity that can be used to access thousands of public and private services.

description: Alphabet’s Google won a reprieve from one of its biggest legal battles in Europe when a Paris court threw out a $1.27 billion bill that France’s tax authority has sought from the search giant for five years of back taxes.
message: The Paris court's decision, covering the years 2005 to 2010, backs Google’s position in a dispute that has dragged on for more than six years, and could have implications for other tax battles in Europe and elsewhere.

description: Got an iPhone 6 or 6s with a draining battery? WSJ's Joanna Stern tells you easy and hard ways to fix the problem now—so you can hold out for the new iPhone models due this fall.
message: Yes, your iPhone 6 is losing battery quicker than it used to. But WSJ's Joanna Stern has ways to get around that. http://on.wsj.com/2t4Nq9W

description: Did Don Jr., a Russian pop star and a lawyer steal the 2016 election?
message: WSJ Opinion: Is it really plausible that Don Jr. was canny enough to coordinate a global plot to rig the election but not canny enough to notice that this plot was detailed in his personal emails?

description: A Senate committee is asking President Trump’s former campaign chairman to testify about a meeting he attended between Trump confidants and a Russian lawyer with ties to the Kremlin.
message: Sen. Chuck Grassley, the Republican head of the Judiciary Committee, said he would be inviting Manafort to a hearing on the issue of foreign lobbying and influence in the U.S.

description: Federal Reserve Chairwoman Janet Yellen told a House panel she expects forces holding down consumer prices to fade in the months ahead, allowing the central bank to stick to its plans for gradual interest-rate increases.
message: Yellen left herself an out, saying the Fed would alter its plans if softer price pressures proved more persistent.

description: U.S. intelligence agencies starting in the spring of 2015 detected conversations in which Russian government officials discussed meetings with associates of Donald Trump, several months before he declared his candidacy for president.
message: In some cases, the Russians in the overheard conversations talked about meetings held outside the U.S. involving Russian government officials and Trump business associates or advisers, according to current and former U.S. officials.

description: Christopher Wray, President Donald Trump’s pick to be the next FBI director, pledged to be an independent leader who would never let politics interfere with the bureau’s investigations.
message: “No one asked me for any kind of loyalty oath,” Wray said. “I sure as heck didn’t offer one.”

description: A new cabinet-level agency could help—if officials have learned the lessons of Homeland Security.
message: WSJ Opinion: At least 11 federal agencies bear significant responsibility for cybersecurity: Congress should merge these disparate cybersecurity programs into one cabinet-level agency that also serves as the focal point for collaboration with the private economy.

description: New Jersey has won its monthslong battle against stricter fishing quotas for summer flounder.
message: Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross approved New Jersey’s rules for summer flounder fishing, which officials implemented earlier this year in defiance of a quota by the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission.

description: After Andy Murray’s quarterfinal loss, title chances for the home crowd at Wimbledon rest on the late-blooming Johanna Konta.
message: Konta is set for a semifinal showdown Thursday with Venus Williams after a quarterfinal win  that seemed to signal a few days of all-out Britmania at Wimbledon.

description: The German government called on Siemens to explain how gas turbines it had sold for use at a Russian power plant got diverted to Crimea, possibly violating EU sanctions in the wake of Moscow’s annexation of the Ukrainian peninsula.
message: The German government said it was closely following efforts to determine what happened with the turbines and said it expected fast answers from Siemens.

description: Amanda Foreman on recent moves to suppress “cultural appropriation” and the need for a free exchange of ideas among societies.
message: “Cultural appropriation” is a leading contender for the most overused phrase of 2017, writes Amanda Foreman.

description: ‘Game of Thrones’ lovers crunch statistics and write computer code to keep track of the plot twists, betrayals, deaths and reappearances of its numerous characters.
message: Like sports, the twists and turns of Game of Thrones can be analyzed (and overanalyzed).

description: Former Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was convicted on corruption charges stemming from the Car Wash probe, the massive graft investigation centered on state-owned oil company Petróleo Brasileiro.
message: Brazil’s ex-president Lula da Silva convicted in corruption probe, gets more than nine years in jail.

description: Tovala, a new twist on healthy meal subscriptions, gives Blue Apron a run for its money, but there’s a catch: You have to buy a new oven.
message: Tovala, a new twist on healthy meal subscriptions, gives Blue Apron a run for its money, but there’s a catch: You have to buy a new oven.

description: A question every organization is desperately trying to answer: Can something as nebulous as “chemistry” be quantified like on-base percentage or ERA?
message: Baseball is desperately trying to answer an age-old question: Whether something as nebulous as “chemistry” be quantified—and then weaponized.

description: Skepticism of electric cars melts a bit more with each new announcement from auto makers. But if they are ever to displace gasoline engines, they must not only keep innovating but outrun fossil fuels where productivity also keeps advancing.
message: Electric cars have come a long way. But they ?still depend too much on public largess to displace gas engines.

description: The Wall Street Journal announced details of a broad editorial reorganization as part of its “WSJ2020” review, creating a new leadership structure with the aim of transforming the 128-year-old newspaper into a mobile-first news operation.
message: The Wall Street Journal is reorganizing its newsroom and creating senior roles. The efforts center on digital and mobile initiatives.

description: Higher rates and larger down payments don’t deter buyers, who don’t believe the government will allow a market collapse.
message: China is trying to curb its booming housing market, but buyers aren't listening. Higher rates and larger down payments aren't slowing the frenzy.

description: Putting on VR goggles and virtually swimming with dolphins can ease some patients’ pain, new research shows. Hospitals across the country are giving VR a try.
message: Ernest “Buck” Shearer, a 40-year-old Cedars-Sinai patient who has endured considerable pain related to Crohn’s disease, took part in a trial last spring and found relief with virtual reality. “It distracts your mind completely,” he says.

description: As he tours America, the Facebook CEO appears at homes and businesses with little notice, asks not to be quoted; not always recognized.
message: Mark Zuckerberg is midway through a “personal challenge” to travel to 30 states he’d never visited, talking to people about the future. The Facebook CEO is showing up at homes and businesses with little notice.

description: Two changes in the screening process now being tested could end nuisances like laptop bans and the 3-ounce rule.
message: Two innovations show how years of research by manufacturers and TSA into ways to improve screening are finally starting to affect checkpoints. But, these innovations could ultimately disappoint.

description: Britney Spears is a rumored to be under consideration for the Super Bowl halftime show, but the Nobel-winning legend should be the pick, writes Jason Gay.
message: Minneapolis music hero Prince would have been the perfect pick for the Super Bowl LII halftime show in Minneapolis, but since Prince is no longer with us, there’s really only one choice: Dylan.

description: NATO and Russian pilots are reviving a Cold War contest of nerves, increasing the risk that airborne close encounters could accidentally spark a conflict.
message: Airborne close encounters, usually meant as a show of force or used to test tactics, revives a dormant game of chicken long played by Soviet and North Atlantic Treaty Organization pilots.

description: Yankees’ rookie Aaron Judge put on a show during the Home Run Derby and is ”the kind of player that can become the face of the game.”
message: Aaron Judge, the hulking behemoth who occupies right field for the New York Yankees, is precisely what baseball has been looking for.

description: A network of dams and locks that make commercial river traffic possible across the U.S. is at risk of failure after decades of underinvestment, potentially causing significant economic damage.
message: “People don’t know they’re getting a $200 million benefit each year moving through these locks and dams on the Monongahela River,” said U.S. Army Corps of Engineers project manager Stephen Fritz.

description: Federal Reserve Chairwoman Janet Yellen visits Capitol Hill this week to testify on monetary policy.
message: One topic that lawmakers could bring up is the Trump administration's first nominee to the Fed’s governing board--Randal Quarles.

description: There are three vacancies on the Federal Reserve Board.
message: How and when President Trump chooses to fill the Fed vacancies is key.

description: Christopher Wray, Donald Trump's nominee for FBI director, faces his confirmation hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee as the Bureau struggles to regain its footing after months of political battering
message: FBI Director Pick Christopher Wray's hearing is likely to be a contentious session exploring the firing of the last director, James Comey, and the relationship between the bureau and the White House.

description: A personal, guided tour to the best scoops and stories every day in The Wall Street Journal, from Editor in Chief Gerard Baker.
message:
Today's top stories: Gerard Baker on Donald Trump Jr.'s emails and more news.
Sign up here for the daily newsletter: http://on.wsj.com/2uRa1nF

description: Nearly every living former chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers is urging President Donald Trump not to impose new steel import curbs in the name of national security, in a letter to be sent to the White House on Wednesday.
message: Some 15 economists who advised past presidents of both parties warn that tariffs “would likely do harm” to U.S. relations with major allies that are top sources of steel imports, including Canada, Brazil, South Korea and Mexico.

description: President Trump defended his son Donald Jr. in morning tweets and attacked the news media, a day after the younger Mr. Trump released documents related to an alleged Russian government offer of help damaging Hillary Clinton’s presidential campaign.
message: Mentioning his son’s appearance on Fox News, the president tweeted: “My son Donald did a good job last night. He was open, transparent and innocent. This is the greatest Witch Hunt in political history. Sad.”

description: Visa Inc. has a new offer for small merchants: take thousands of dollars from the card giant to upgrade their payment technology. In return, the businesses must stop accepting cash.
message: Visa plans to give $10,000 apiece to up to 50 restaurants and food vendors to pay for  technology and marketing costs, as long as the businesses pledge to start what Visa calls a “journey to cashless.”

description: Federal Reserve Chairwoman Janet Yellen heads to Capitol Hill to address the House Financial Services Committee in her twice-yearly Humphrey Hawkins testimony.
message: Lawmakers are expected to question Yellen on the Fed’s plans to raise interest rate during the hearing.

description: Banks have kept consumer deposit yields low through several Federal Reserve rate hikes—and some banks are wondering when consumers will start demanding more.
message: Interest rates are rising. So why aren’t bank customers demanding higher interest on their deposits? This is the dilemma confronting banks.

description: China faces a moment of truth in its own backyard. So far, its approach on Pyongyang lines up poorly with its ambition to assume greater global leadership.
message: Is China ready to be a world leader like the U.S.? Its approach to North Korea suggests it isn't.

description: A looming global diamond shortage is driving a small band of adventurous miners to brave bone-chilling winds at the world’s highest mines to extract stones that are worth as much as 20 times the global average.
message: A surge in demand and looming shortage for the stones is reshaping mining in one of the world’s poorest countries.

description: Christopher Wray, President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the FBI, is set to appear before lawmakers Wednesday morning in what is likely to be a contentious session exploring the firing of the last director, James Comey, and the relationship between the bureau and the White House.
message: Democrats are likely to press Mr. Wray about Mr. Comey’s ouster, which came amid the investigation into Russian meddling in the 2016 election and potential coordination between the Trump campaign and Russia.

description: The emails that Donald Trump Jr. disclosed  provided new fuel to critics of the Trump administration by making the prospect of possible collusion with Russia appear more concrete.
message: WSJ's Gerald F. Seib explains the political impact of the emails.

description: Career websites like Glassdoor have become regular reading for job seekers. Now chief executives are increasingly perusing their online reviews to find out what employees think of them—to evaluate policies and even to talk back.
message: Public-yet-personal critiques are prompting more company bosses to track and respond to reviews.

description: The administration faced a July 12 deadline to decide if sanctions relief initiated by the Obama administration in January would become permanent.
message: The Trump administration said it is delaying a decision on whether to lift sanctions on Sudan by three months.

description: States are restricting how and when dicamba can be sprayed and ratcheting up fines for misuse.
message: Crop damage from a powerful herbicide is spreading across the southern U.S.

description: European diplomats say they are increasingly concerned the Trump administration will stretch out its review of the Iranian nuclear deal, undermining the agreement by curbing the economic benefits designed to ensure Iran’s compliance.
message: European officials have remained publicly upbeat about the U.S. remaining a party to the deal, but diplomats privately voice serious concerns about where the U.S. review is headed.

description: As Tesla begins a launch of its first mass-market car, the company said it plans to triple its capacity to repair vehicles, adding 1,400 technicians, dozens of new service centers and hundreds of maintenance vans.
message: The new vans will come equipped with espresso machines and snacks for the customers.

description: Publishers are calling on the U.S. Congress to allow them to negotiate collectively with Google and Facebook, as the duo increasingly dominate digital advertising and news distribution online.
message: The News Media Alliance says antiquated antitrust laws have had “the unintended effect of preserving and protecting Google and Facebook’s dominant position,” by limiting publishers’ ability to push for changes together.

description: Surprised by the disclosures involving President Donald Trump’s son, some White House aides fear the story will make it increasingly difficult to advance the president’s policy agenda.
message: “This is more significant and serious than anything else we’ve seen,” one administration official said.

description: Facebook has spent years developing two of the world’s most popular messaging apps. Now, with slowing revenue growth in its core product, it wants to cash in.
message: Facebook says Messenger, its chat app, is now used by 1.2 billion people every month.

description: Jia Yueting likes to say that Apple is outdated, China’s big tech companies are innovation killers and his company is the real disrupter. But now, his dreams are fading away due to a cash crunch and worried investors.
message: China’s tech boom has been looking like a bubble for some time.

description: Parents naturally zoom in on what their children are doing wrong, but shifting to focus on a child’s strengths is more effective.
message: Why do we zoom in on our children’s faults and find it so hard to resist the urge to criticize?

description: North Korea’s recently tested long-range missile might not be able to survive the intense heat and vibration of re-entering the atmosphere, said South Korea’s intelligence agency.
message: When it re-enters the Earth’s atmosphere on its descent, the warhead is exposed to temperatures of thousands of degrees and extreme vibration.

description: Julian Velard, a Brooklyn musician and 2017 artist-in-residence at Joe’s Pub in Manhattan, says the theme of failure runs through much his new work.
message: Brooklyn based singer-songwriter Julian Velard has found a new muse and her name is failure.

description: D.A. Pennebaker, 91, is a documentary filmmaker whose films include “Dont Look Back,” “Monterey Pop,” “ Ziggy Stardust, ” “The War Room” and, most recently, “Unlocking the Cage.”
message: Growing up in boarding schools and rarely seeing his parents led to a career as a counterculture documentarian for filmmaker D.A. Pennebaker.

description: The hope that the story of Russia’s role in the 2016 presidential election would quickly shrivel up and blow away has dimmed significantly says Gerald F. Seib.
message:
For months, the hope in President Donald Trump’s world—sometimes realistic, sometimes strained—was that the story of Russia’s role in the 2016 presidential election would quickly shrivel up and blow away.

That dream died on Tuesday, writes Gerald F. Seib.

description: A Chinese startup that sells facial recognition systems to police secured venture-capital funding that values it at more than $1.5 billion, underscoring the sector’s emergence as one of technology’s hottest areas of interest.
message: The latest sign of how facial recognition technology is becoming such a hot area in China.

description: Correspondence released Tuesday by the president’s eldest son suggests a possible effort to influence the Trump campaign by Russia’s prosecutor general, one of the nation’s most powerful men.
message: The Trump Jr. correspondence appears to link efforts to influence the campaign to one of Russia’s most powerful men. Here are more details.

description: Much of the first half of the baseball season has revolved around one story: the enormous rise in home runs.
message: Teams are on pace to blast 6,126 home runs this year, which would shatter the current record set in 2000 by more than 400.

description: The funeral for slain New York Police Department officer Miosotis Familia put on display new rifts in the relationship between Mayor Bill de Blasio and the city’s police force.
message: Some officers appeared to turn their backs on the mayor as he eulogized Officer Familia.

description: After decades of growth, the self-storage industry is poised for a slowdown, according to real estate research firm Green Street Advisors.
message: The age of tiny electronics and minimalism may put a dent in the self-storage business.

description: A Senate provision could hurt U.S. oil firms working outside Russia.
message: WSJ Opinion: A Senate provision could hurt U.S. oil firms working outside Russia.

description: New emails disclosed Tuesday concerning Donald Trump Jr.’s 2016 meeting with a Russian lawyer fill in details that could be legally problematic for the president’s son, say legal experts.
message: The new emails don’t amount to a slam-dunk indictment of Donald Trump Jr., legal experts say, but could help build a criminal or civil-enforcement case.

description: Paul Singer’s Elliott Management is ramping up pressure on Berkshire Hathaway with the threat of a rival offer, arguing the $9 billion offer last week for bankrupt Energy Future Holdings isn’t high enough.
message: Will Elliott Management push Warren Buffett to raise its bid for Energy Future? The Oracle of Omaha's letters and annual report reveal his thinking.

description: The airport in Charleston, W.Va., points up the U.S.’s infrastructure needs—an aging facility with a long wish list of upgrades that is a big ask given current funding levels for facilities nationally.
message: Think your airport is bad? Did the runway slide down a hill onto a church?

description: Venus Williams continued to impress at Wimbledon, advancing to the semifinals with a 6-3, 7-5 victory against Jelena Ostapenko. Next up is British star Johanna Konta.
message: Venus Williams, at 37, is two wins away from claiming her first Grand Slam title in almost 10 years.

description: Some of the tennis’ tallest players—Tomas Berdych (6’5”), Sam Querrey (6’6”) and Milos Raonic (6’5”)—are looking to breakthrough at Wimbledon, where bending for low shots can be difficult.
message: The best tennis players fall within a Goldilocks zone of not-too-tall and not-too-small.

description: Maduro frees a dissident from prison, casting a light on fissures within the country’s Chavismo elite.
message: WSJ Opinion: Last week the Supreme Court attempted to usurp Attorney General Luisa Ortega Diaz’s power by appointing a new deputy attorney general. The illicitly appointed deputy was then smuggled into the Public Ministry in the trunk of a car, writes Vanessa Neumann.

description: How do retirees respond to life without a regular paycheck? Research reveals the unexpected answers.
Congressional Republicans reacted cautiously to the release of Donald Trump Jr.’s emails, with most deferring to investigators on Capitol Hill and in the Justice Department.
message: Many GOP lawmakers  appeared eager to discuss items other than Donald Trump Jr.'s emails. However, Sen. Orrin Hatch (R., Utah) dismissed the younger Mr. Trump’s revelations as “a bunch of bunk” and reiterated his support for the president.

description: The release of emails purporting to show Russia offered help to President Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign is ramping up calls for Congress to pass a bill sanctioning Moscow for its interference in the election.
message: The Trump administration’s position is being undercut by revelations from investigations into Moscow’s meddling in the 2016 presidential campaign, including the president’s son’s emails.

description: A $10,000 grant for theater ‘celebrating the saguaro cactus’? The National Endowment said yes.
message: WSJ Opinion: A new report from Open the Books provides an eye-opening look into the size of the NEA and NEH tab that the taxpayers have been picking up. Doubtless many initiatives could be worthy, but a lot of the funded projects are inane, repellent or both, writes Roger Kimball.

description: The military plane that crashed in Mississippi and killed all 16 aboard was carrying a group of elite Marine troops headed to California for specialized training, U.S. defense officials said.
message: The crash late Monday evening took the lives of 15 Marines and one Navy sailor. The plane was carrying a a group of Marines from what’s known as the Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command.

description: Study after study shows that college students are terrible at keeping track of how much debt they are racking up in school, so states are working to make the cost of higher education crystal clear—and there are signs that the moves are slowing runaway borrowing.
message: Some college students are choosing to borrow less cash for school--after being shown just how much they already owe.

description: Summer means no iPhone buying. Joanna Stern shares tips and tricks to help your failing phone make it to the upgrade.
message: Our haggard iPhone 6 and 6s: It turns out most of their common problems can be fixed—with money and/or time.

description: Force ruling elites to choose between North Korea and American colleges for their kids.
message: WSJ Opinion: If China’s ruling elite were forced to choose between supporting North Korea and their children’s access to American universities, is it all that hard to see where they would come down?

description: Spireworks, downloaded by invitation only, lets users change the lights on two tower spires from red to blue to orange—and add sparkles. ‘It doesn’t feel like something I should have access to.’
message: Pulling out your phone to change the lights of the Manhattan skyline. "I just had to have it," said one app fan.

description: The IOC voted to award the next two Summer Games simultaneously in September, a dramatic move as the committee tries to position the event for the future
message: Tuesday's move all but guarantees the 2024 and 2028 Summer Olympics will be in Paris and Los Angeles, with Paris likely first.

description: The U.S. and Qatar signed an agreement in Doha to crack down on terrorist financing, as Secretary of State Rex Tillerson shuttles around the Persian Gulf to resolve a weekslong conflict between four Arab states and Qatar.
message: Under a new agreement, the U.S. and Qatar will step up efforts to track down terrorist funding sources and will do more to collaborate and share information.

description: Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell said the chamber would begin its August break two weeks late, as he aims to pass a health-care bill that likely will retain two Affordable Care Act taxes on high-income households.
message: The delay to the August recess came as people familiar with the Senate GOP health-care legislation said it likely will retain both of the Affordable Care Act’s taxes that affect high-income households.

description: Major internet companies are preparing to launch online protests Wednesday over Republican efforts to roll back Obama-era net neutrality rules. It’s worked in the past, but will it now?
message: Big internet companies worry that without strong net-neutrality rules, telecom-service providers could use internet fast lanes to push their own online services.

description: The GOP Senate needs to stop Democratic abuse of the rules.
message: WSJ Opinion: Senate Democrats are abusing Senate rules to undermine the executive branch, and Republicans need to restore normal order, writes the Editorial Board.

description: Intel on Tuesday brought to market a new generation of chips used in the servers that run data centers, firing back at competitors who lately have moved to challenge its hegemony in its most profitable market
message: Intel makes most of its revenue on processors for personal computers, but the powerful server chips bring higher prices and profit margins.

description: Traditional retail stocks like Macy’s Inc. were pummeled yet again on Monday, the latest reminder that stockpickers need to throw out the old rulebook when it comes to valuing brick-and-mortar stores.
message: How good news for Amazon spells bad news for other retailers.

description: Time Inc. is considering a major rebranding that could include a corporate name change, as the publisher tries to position itself as a modern media company with growing digital and video ventures.
message: Senior executives at Time Inc. recently met to discuss a potential rebranding of the company that could include changing the publisher’s corporate name.

description: Federal Reserve Chairwoman Janet Yellen heads to Capitol Hill on Wednesday to address the House Financial Services Committee in her twice-yearly Humphrey Hawkins testimony and to take questions from lawmakers.
message: Fed chief Yellen to give twice-yearly Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.

description: Takata recalled an additional 2.7 million air bags in the U.S. that are at risk of rupturing, adding to a mushrooming safety crisis that forced the Japanese company to seek bankruptcy protection.
message: The latest group of air bags being recalled are installed in Ford, Nissan and Mazda vehicles.

description: In the age of Netflix movies, HBO TV shows and Marvel big-screen series, the 120-year-old definition of a feature film is defunct
message: Netflix, Marvel and HBO are blurring the lines between the big screen and small, between big-budget TV and mid-budget movies.

description: The day after announcing Islamic State’s defeat in Mosul, Iraqis turned to the enormous challenges of rebuilding and resettling the country’s second-largest city.
message: After recapturing Mosul from Islamic State, Iraq faces the colossal challenge of rebuilding and resettling the country’s second-largest city.

description: A Chicagoan loved the Irish band enough to track down one of the Trabants used in the band’s early-’90s Zoo TV tour.
message: Remember the tiny car from U2’s ‘One’ video? This fan tracked one down.

description: A software engineer, business owner, and self-described introvert emulated the communication styles, dress and approaches others use to make good impressions on clients or colleagues.
message: Networking isn't easy, but it can be learned. Start with some interesting shoes.

description: Germany has asked European governments for help in finding and prosecuting rioters who left a trail of destruction in Hamburg during the weekend’s Group of 20 summit.
message: Germany is calling for help in tackling 'riot tourism.'

description: The president’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., attended a meeting last June to discuss allegedly incriminating information about Hillary Clinton he was told was being offered as part of Russian government support of his father’s candidacy, according to emails he released.
message: The release of the emails offers clear evidence that senior officials in the Trump camp entertained offers of Russia’s help in last year’s campaign.

description: Rising home prices have turned the great home-equity-line reset into a small setback rather than a disaster for the banking industry.
message: The home-equity lines that banks made in the go-go days of the housing boom are resetting, sometimes adding hundreds of dollars to a customer's monthly payment. But the banks say they expect just a small setback, not a disaster, thanks in part to rising home prices.

description: A Chinese startup that sells facial recognition systems to police secured venture-capital funding that values it at more than $1.5 billion, underscoring the sector’s emergence as one of technology’s hottest areas of interest.
message: SenseTime Co., which provides surveillance systems using facial recognition to Chinese law enforcement agencies, raised $410 million in new funding from investors, lifting it to so-called unicorn status with a value of more than $1 billion.

description: Company pays stipends of $5,000 to $400,000 for research supporting business practices that face regulatory scrutiny. A ‘wish list’ of topics.
message: Google supports professors who write academic papers favorable to its business practices, emails show

description: As Tesla begins a launch of its first mass-market car, the company said it plans to triple its capacity to repair vehicles, adding 1,400 technicians, dozens of new service centers and hundreds of maintenance vans.
message: As Tesla braces for the most critical test in its 14-year history, it's planning to triple its capacity to repair vehicles.

description: Women entrepreneurs receive a tiny fraction venture capital funds, and new research points to a surprising reason why: the questions investors ask female founders.
message: While women have founded nearly 40% of all privately held companies in the U.S., they have fetched just 3% of all venture capital.

description: Career websites like Glassdoor have become regular reading for job seekers. Now chief executives are increasingly perusing their online reviews to find out what employees think of them—to evaluate policies and even to talk back.
message: More CEOs are peeking at their own performance reviews on anonymous websites.

description: Consultants who help store owners wring concessions from landlords are seeing brisk business these days, another ripple of the shifting retail landscape across the U.S. economy.
message: As store owners scrutinize their store footprints, they are turning increasingly to professionals who can help them get better deals from landlords.

description: This week’s U.S. Women’s Open won’t be the last major championship at a course owned by Donald Trump. Despite criticism, professional golf on the whole is finding that it doesn’t need to distance itself from the president.
message: Despite criticism, this week’s U.S. Women’s Open likely won’t be the last major championship at a Trump course.

description: A personal, guided tour to the best scoops and stories every day in The Wall Street Journal, from Editor in Chief Gerard Baker.
message:
Today's top stories: Gerard Baker on tighter North Korea sanctions, Trump's Fed bank regulator nomination and more news. 
Sign up here for the daily newsletter: http://on.wsj.com/2uMGvzH

description: Dalian Wanda’s sale of its theme parks and hotels to developer Sunac China Holdings has an unusual twist: Wanda is helping Sunac finance almost half of the deal.
message: The unusual twist to Wanda’s $9 billion sale of its theme parks and hotels: The company is helping finance almost half of the deal.

description: A handful of startups are betting they can help apartment-building owners covert empty units into hotel rooms, a controversial practice that could help landlords generate more revenue.
message: Airbnb for landlords: Startups help owners get in on home-sharing trend.

description: Last August, Maryland’s elections board discovered someone was probing the state’s online voter-registration system. The intrusion failed, but the hacking attempt prompted new precautions and concerns from lawmakers.
message: Attempted hack of Maryland's voter-registration system prompts precautions--and lawmakers' questions.

description: Brandless, an e-commerce startup, is betting shoppers would rather pay $3 for generic versions of household staples rather than buy Colgate, Heinz and other big-name goods.
message: A new online retailer is betting it can get American shoppers to break up with big brands from Colgate to Heinz.

description: As crop damage from a powerful herbicide spreads across the southern U.S., states are restricting how and when dicamba can be sprayed and ratcheting up fines for misuse. Arkansas, which has received nearly 600 complaints of dicamba-related damage this year, banned its use or sale for 120 days.
message: Farmers across the southern U.S. say a powerful herbicide is drifting from their neighbors’ fields and damaging crops.

description: China faces a moment of truth in its own backyard. So far, its approach on Pyongyang lines up poorly with its ambition to assume greater global leadership.
message: Is China ready to be a world leader? Its approach on North Korea suggests otherwise.

description: European diplomats say they are increasingly concerned the Trump administration will stretch out its review of the Iranian nuclear deal, undermining the agreement by curbing the economic benefits designed to ensure Iran’s compliance.
message: The limbo over the deal could strain U.S. ties with Europe, where the governments of France, Germany, and the U.K., as well as the European Union, helped negotiate the deal and strongly support it.

description: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway is relying less on stock picking for its future, as its latest energy bid signals.
message: Berkshire has undergone a “gradual shift from a company obtaining most of its gains from investment activities to one that grows in value by owning businesses."

description: Three years after Islamic State captured the Iraqi city of Mosul, the country's armed forces have all but liberated the city from the extremist group.
message: The return of Mosul to Iraqi control represents a significant symbolic and strategic victory over Islamic State, but the group remains active in parts of Iraq and Syria and is far from defeated.

description: North Korea’s recently tested long-range missile might not be able to survive the intense heat and vibration of re-entering the atmosphere, said South Korea’s intelligence agency.
message: South Korea's spy agency says a North Korean warhead may not be able to withstand atmospheric re-entry.

description: Samsonite International, the world’s largest luggage maker by volume, is looking to double its market share in the next decade, by widening its product range, pushing into smart luggage, and focusing on bags designed for women.
message: Samsonite is widening its product range, pushing into smart luggage, and focusing on women’s bags.

description: Singapore state investment firm Temasek Holdings said it sold more assets than it bought in the last financial year for the first time in nine years, as it refocused on private equity and moved away from public markets where valuations are high.
message: Temasek's total portfolio value up 13.6% to US$198.6 billion in the last financial year.

description: Rafael Nadal falls in a five-set marathon at Wimbledon, while Johanna Konta and Andy Murray provide thrills on tennis’ most frenzied day.
message: Rafa Nadal falls in a five-set thriller in a Maniac Monday at Wimbledon.

description: Pearson is selling a 22% stake in Penguin Random House for $1 billion to its joint-venture partner, German media company Bertelsmann.
message: Pearson will still retain a 25% in the business after the sale.

description: A look at the key people who attended or helped arrange a meeting between members of Donald Trump’s inner circle and a Russian lawyer in June 2016.
message: A look at the key people who attended or helped arrange the meeting.

description: President Donald Trump’s eldest son retained a private attorney on Monday and said he would work with congressional investigators who have sought his testimony as part of ongoing probes into whether the president’s campaign colluded with Moscow to influence the election.
message: President Trump’s eldest son engaged in a “very short meeting from which there was absolutely no follow up” when he met with a Russian lawyer with Kremlin ties, the White House said.

description: Iraq’s U.S.-backed prime minister declared victory over Islamic State in Mosul on Monday, but Iran is shaping up to be one of the biggest winners in the struggle with Washington for influence in Baghdad and across the region.
message: Islamic State’s losses in Mosul also are expected to make it easier for Shiite-majority Iran to ship weapons through northern Iraq and neighboring Syria to the Hezbollah militia Iran supports in Lebanon.

description: Legal experts say it is far from clear whether Donald Trump Jr.’s 2016 meeting with a Kremlin-connected Russian lawyer crossed a legal line.
message: Law experts say it’s unclear if Donald Trump Jr.’s meeting with a Russian lawyer crossed legal line.

description: Microsoft plans to put its lobbying and financial muscle behind a long-shot technology that taps unused television bandwidth to bring broadband access to underserved areas of America.
message: The technology Microsoft is championing harnesses unused bandwidth between TV channels to wirelessly deliver access.

description: A Marine transport plane crashed in Mississippi on Monday, military officials said, as local media reported that the crash killed at least twelve individuals.
message: At least 12 people were killed in the plane crash.

description: Here’s some of the things Randal Quarles, Trump’s nomination for a key Fed bank regulator post, has said over the years about regulatory policies for big banks.
message: Here are some of the things Fed nominee Randal Quarles has said over the years.

description: A U.S. soldier stationed in Hawaii has been charged with providing material support to ISIS, according to a criminal complaint filed Monday in the U.S. District Court in Honolulu.
message: A U.S. soldier stationed in Hawaii has been charged with providing material support to Islamic State.

After their first child, Noah, was diagnosed in 2009 with Batten disease, a deadly childhood illness, Tracy and Jen VanHoutan began a tireless quest to save their son.

They worked internationally with scientists to find therapies where none existed, lobbied Congress and the FDA, and helped raise more than $1.5 million in the search for a cure.

Earlier this year, the unrelenting efforts of the suburban Chicago couple paid off when the FDA approved the first known drug found to dramatically slow the effects of Batten disease. 

"I can honestly say it wouldn't have happened if it weren't for them," said Julia Jenkins, executive director of the EveryLife Foundation for Rare Diseases.
 
Sadly, for the VanHoutans, it didn't happen fast enough.

Noah Scott VanHoutan died in March 2016, just shy of his 12th birthday. And Laine VanHoutan, now 11, is in hospice care. 

"We prayed for a miracle," said Jacqueline Farnaus, Jen VanHoutan's mother. "Maybe the miracle for Noah and Laine happened in a different way. Maybe it's that they were the saviors for other kids."

They’re placed by companies called lead generators, and they work by collecting and distributing personal information about consumers online. So while Google says it bans ads that guarantee foreclosure prevention or promise short-term loans without conveying accurate loan terms, lead generators may direct consumers to a landing page where they’re asked to input sensitive identifiable information. Scarborough, also known as Joe Scarborough of MSNBC’s Morning Joe, is slated to release his debut EP, Mystified, on Friday, June 23rd. The album is the first official musical offering from the award-winning television personality, with more original music to come over the next 4 years. Mystified will be available for streaming and purchase on Friday, June 23rd.

On his new music, Joe says, “I’ve got a hell of a lot of songs to get out there, so I’ll be releasing them in waves with an EP every month for the next four years. I may take a quick rest after releasing my first 200 songs.”

Scarborough has spent the last year holed up in studios recording 50 of his 400 original songs. His band has played regular electrifying shows in standing-room-only club settings in Scarborough’s Upper Westside neighborhood. The shows compelled Scarborough to double down on his music mission.

Releasing 200 songs in four years may seem like a monumental challenge for a public figure who hosts the most important political show in America and writes a weekly print column for the Washington Post, but it is all in a day’s work for a songwriter who penned a 36-song musical during his first year of law school.

After listening, you will find yourself agreeing with Billboard that Scarborough does, indeed, have chops. And if you catch Scarborough live, you may understand why fashion legend Andre Leon Talley believes the great Andy Warhol would wholeheartedly approve of this year’s most surprising debut artist.

After more than a dozen years at Fox News, I have decided to pursue a new challenge. This was a tough decision for me because I love this show, our staff, my crew, my colleagues here at Fox – and you, all of you.

Over a dozen years ago I started at Fox News in a job that would change my life. Now, I have decided to end my time at FNC, incredibly enriched for the experiences I've had.
